To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a set of equations to evaluate the photon management properties for the single-frequency and the full-spectrum light harvesting of silicon nanowires.
we established comprehensive equations to evaluate the photon management properties (PM) of silicon nanowires (SiNW) and derived four extra formulas for the optimal size of the SiNW.
we have derived a comprehensive set of exact equations that can predict the light harvesting performance of SiNW, which can be applied to design and optimize the SiNW-based photovoltaic devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comprehensive equations for the PM properties, such as the resonant wavelengths, the light-harverting efficiency, of SiNW.
the comprehensive equations for the PM properties, which is the basis for the quantitative estimation and rational design of SiNW-based devices.

the comprehensive theoretical study of the photon management properties (PMPs) in SiNWs, which are of vital importance to its applications in nanowire photodetectors (PDs), nanowire chemical sensors (NS), nanowire waveguides (WG), nanowire optical switches (OS), nanowire solar cells (SC), and nanowire lasers (Laser).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the equations derived in this work can be used to predict the light-harving efficiency and resonant wavelength of SiNWs with high accuracy.

we have established a set of equations to estimate the PM properties of a SiNW with any shape and size, which can reproduce the majority of the reported theoretical and experimental results, and can be used as a guide to the rational design of SiNW-based nanophotonic devices.

we have established the exact comprehensive equations to estimate the PM properties of silicon nanorod, based on theoretical calculations, which can reproduce majority of reported experimental and theoretical data with only ~5%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a set of efficient equations to estimate the photon management properties for SiNW, which can reproduce majority of reported results with only ~ 5% error deviations.
we established the first set of equations to estimate the PM properties of a single SiNW in full spectrum.
the equations we established can be used as a design tool for the PM properties in SiNW-based devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light-harving efficiency of SiNW is a function of the ratio between the diameter (d) of SiNW and its RW.
the SiNW’s RW can be tuned from visible to mid-infrared region, while its light-harvest efficiency at RW can reach ~100%.
the PM performance of SiNW can be optimized by tuning its size.
